**Finding: MISSING** — no insurance clause exists in this Agreement.

**What I checked**
- Text searches for "insurance," "insur," and "coverage" returned zero hits document-wide.
- Read the full General Provisions article (§10, p0059–p0070) — notices, no joint venture, assignment, waiver, governing law, severability, survival, entire agreement, headings — no insurance provision.
- Read §§1.4–5.3 and §§6–9 to confirm no insurance obligation is buried in the operative or warranty sections.

**Why it matters here (direction check)**
This is an obligation we want imposed on the counterparty, not one that binds us, so inserting it is appropriate. HDI is a genuine hosting/services vendor touching our data:
- stores and operates the Site on HDI's computer system (p0009);
- collects and exports customer order data (p0010);
- has access to Company Content, user information and customer e-mail lists as Confidential Information (p0044, p0048).

With zero coverage for a vendor processing customer data, the document sits below the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) and approaches the playbook's walk-away line.

**Redline (validated ok:true)**
New **Section 10.9 Insurance** inserted after p0070, at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; E&O USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M covering HDI's hosting and data processing; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request; maintained through the term plus one year. Placed in the miscellaneous section per the redline guidance, and the comment flags the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback as an available landing zone.

Confidence: 0.9. One drafting note carried in the rationale rather than the clause: the Agreement has no defined term "Customer Data," so the cyber limb is tied to the existing defined term "Confidential Information" plus customer data. Separately, the existing numbering already contains a duplicate "10.7" (p0068 and p0069) — I numbered the new clause 10.9 to follow 10.8, but the article may warrant a renumbering pass.
